title: Shop - Weak JWT None Algorithm (Easy)
description: Gain unauthorized administrative access to the VulnShop Executive Portal (/api/admin/dashboard) by exploiting the insecure acceptance of the 'none' algorithm in JWT authentication.
hints: Inspect the JWT token structure (Header.Payload.Signature) sent to the application.
The 'alg' parameter in the JWT header can be changed to 'none'. In unsecured implementations, the server will skip signature verification if the signature component is omitted.

title: Shop - Weak JWT Secret Brute Force (Medium)
description: The server now rejects 'none' algorithm JWTs, but signs tokens using a weak dictionary HMAC secret. Crack the secret key and forge a valid administrator token to access /api/admin/dashboard.
hints: Obtain a valid user token (e.g. by logging in or registering a customer account) and inspect its HMAC-SHA256 signature.
Use a wordlist attack tool like hashcat (-m 16500), john, or a simple script to crack common weak secrets like 'secret123', then re-sign with username 'admin'.

title: Shop - Weak JWT Header Parameter Confusion (Hard)
description: The server uses a strong random HMAC secret, but inspects JWT header parameters such as 'kid' (Key ID) without input sanitization or accepts embedded 'jwk' keys. Exploit parameter confusion to forge an administrative token.
hints: Check the default token issued in Hard mode. Notice the 'kid' parameter pointing to a key path.
What happens if the 'kid' header parameter is pointed to a predictable or empty file such as '/dev/null'? Or what if an embedded 'jwk' object with a known key is provided?

title: Shop - No Login Rate Limiting (Easy)
description: The administrator account has a standard weak password and the login endpoint (/api/login) enforces no rate limiting or lockout mechanisms. Brute force the login credentials to capture the flag.
hints: The administrator username is 'admin'. Try top common passwords (e.g. 'admin123', 'password', 'welcome123').
Because there are no rate limits in Easy mode, automated credential attempts can be sent as quickly as desired.

title: Shop - Header-Bypass Rate Limiting (Medium)
description: The login endpoint now enforces a rate limiter blocking clients after 5 failed attempts. However, client IP detection trusts spoofable HTTP request headers. Bypass the rate limiter to find the administrator password.
hints: After 5 failed attempts from an IP address, the server responds with HTTP 429 Too Many Requests.
Examine which HTTP headers reverse proxies use to identify client IPs (e.g. X-Forwarded-For, Client-IP). Rotating this header resets the rate limit bucket.

title: Shop - Timing/Response Attack (Hard)
description: In Hard mode, the primary administrator account uses an unguessable password. However, a hidden staff user exists with a dictionary password. Exploit login response timing discrepancies to enumerate existing users, then authenticate to capture the flag.
hints: Compare the response time of /api/login for valid usernames versus non-existent usernames. Notice that cryptographic verification delays response times for real accounts.
Check common service and staff usernames like 'support', 'staff', 'sales', or 'guest'. Once identified, test top dictionary passwords against that account.

title: Shop - Predictable Reset Token MD5 (Easy)
description: The password reset mechanism (/api/forgot-password) generates deterministic, predictable reset tokens based on MD5 hashing of the username. Reset the administrator's password to capture the flag.
hints: Request a password reset for 'admin'. Analyze how the reset token is formatted.
The token is simply md5(username). Compute md5('admin') and submit it to /api/reset-password along with your desired new password.

title: Shop - Predictable Reset Timestamp (Medium)
description: The password reset token is now generated using a timestamp-based hash: sha1(username + unix_timestamp_seconds). Narrow the time window to predict the valid token and reset the administrator's password.
hints: The token is generated at the exact moment /api/forgot-password is called. Check the server's Date response header or record your client timestamp.
Compute sha1('admin' + timestamp) for seconds surrounding the request timestamp (e.g. +/- 5 seconds) to find the valid reset token.

title: Shop - Host Header Poisoning Reset (Hard)
description: In Hard mode, reset tokens are cryptographically random. However, the password reset email construction trusts user-supplied Host / X-Forwarded-Host headers. Exploit Host Header Poisoning to intercept the administrator's reset token and reset their password.
hints: Check the simulated email outbox at /api/emails. Notice how the reset URL inside the email body is formed.

Send a forgot-password request with a modified 'Host' or 'X-Forwarded-Host' header (e.g. 'attacker.local'). Check the outgoing email outbox to verify that the generated link was poisoned with your host, then submit that token to /api/reset-password.
